content.text: : cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
